scenarios.name: passive-enum-to-names-file
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric precisely with amass enum then amass subs -names -o plus thorough verification steps, while B uses entirely different tools (subfinder, assetfinder, puredns) and never runs the required amass enum/subs commands.

scenarios.name: fix-v4-style-command-for-v5
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers every rubric point: it says intel, -json and -o are removed, that results live in the asset database and are read with subs, it seeds with `enum -asn 64496 -cidr 198.51.100.0/24` and it says -passive is deprecated because passive is the default; Response B hedges, routes scope through a config file instead of the -asn/-cidr flags, doesn't say passive is the default, and only partly covers the database and subs point.

scenarios.name: track-new-assets-and-graph
scenarios.rationale: A re-runs `amass enum`, uses `track -since` with the correct format, runs `viz` with `-d3 -dot -gexf -o`, and converts the DOT file with `dot -Tpng`, which covers the whole rubric. B never re-runs `enum`, splits into v3 and v4 branches, and its v4 SQLite and DOT-building steps are speculative and don't match the rubric, though it does include the `track -since` format, `viz -dot` and `dot -Tpng`.
